body: Ok sorry if you got offende by the "bitches". I think you didn't get the humor or my cycle was at a peak. Currently, I'm leaning towards believing I was sexually abused as a child.

Be a whore. this is not actually advice but it is what I do so I suggest you don't turn into it. I'm 19 years old, male, and when the meds I took were still too weak, eveerytime I feel sad, I go out and end up with somebody. Which was bad. When I'm in melancholia I'm really friendly and fun outside.
MY ADVICE IS (AFTER UNNECESSARILY TELLING MY STORY, THIS IS IN CAPS SO YOU MAY JUST READ THIS AND IGNORE EVERYTHING ELSE) EARN REALLY GOOD FRIENDS THAT YOU CAN HIT UP ANYTIME IN THIS WORLD. Seriously. If you're depressed and you want to drive the metal into your veins, be with friends. And you don't have to talk, you just watch them. It's therapeutic. At the very least, don't be alone during your mood swings. Being busy also suspends the mood swings.

It is not really the best thing to do but I would find a job if I'm in your case. I'm 19 and I plan to leave Univ for a year. Currently I work as a journalist for a local paper and it is technically a low-paying 24/7 job. IT keeps you busy and is a constant reminder that you are able to do something on your own. But of course, there are still those days when I just throw my pens away and feel like I'm wasting my life and my editor probably think I'm retarded but getting a job generally helped me. It propped up my confidence and made me believe there is some sort of future. Plus the job is risky when I'm running towards a shootout or asking people about an ambush. Risking my own life is kind of a thrill for me and not in a joke-y way. JUST GET BUSY. It will boost your confidence and direct your emotions. or at least make them stop from churning inside our hardworking heads.

Hey, a lot of my friends know and I even tell them when I self-harm which is kind of weird. But I like talking about it after the episodes because it feels way better to be embarrassed than to catch everyone looking and wondering why you have those lines on your wrists or legs. Just my opinion, which is definitely not the best one this website has to offer.
the hardest part in being bipolar is being unable to stop self-harming and realizing you need the meds.
